archetype.name: Better Than Its Record (defense-first)
archetype.definition: A team whose efficiency, fifth in net EPA, says contender. Its 6-4 record carries the weight of bad special teams, loose ball security and three losses by four points or fewer, and the identity has shifted from last year's high-powered offense to a front that controls the run on both sides of the ball.

report.headline: Top-five efficiency, 6-4 record — and now the defense must carry a depleted offense.
report.take:
These Rams are not the 2025 team that led the league in scoring and net EPA. That version won with Stafford and the passing game (second in offensive EPA, 30.5 points a game). This one is built on two lines of scrimmage. The defense ranks fourth in EPA allowed and second in rush EPA allowed by play-by-play. It gets off the field on third down (31.6% allowed, fourth) and rarely gives up anything deep (third in deep-pass EPA allowed). On offense the line has allowed the lowest pressure rate and the lowest stuff rate in the league. The offense itself has slid to around league-average-plus: eleventh in EPA, with success rate (fifth) running ahead of its explosiveness.

The record lags the play, and the reasons are mostly the kind that don't repeat on schedule. Winds over expected sits at -0.96. The point differential implies seven wins, not six. The losses include a 30-26 game in Denver, a 37-34 shootout with Buffalo and an 18-16 home loss to Arizona as a 12.5-point favorite. Special teams have bled 3.22 EPA a game, 30th in the league. The offense has turned it over 15 times, and only the Buffalo game was clean. Fix even one of those and this is an 8-2 team. That is why they have covered in every win and why the market still treats them as a favorite against a Green Bay team with the same record.

Two numbers mislead. The pass defense ranks 28th in passing yards allowed per game but sixth in pass EPA allowed. Much of that yardage came in games the Rams controlled: Las Vegas threw for 308 and Washington for 274 in losses. Opponents are accumulating, not scoring. The real hole on defense is the pass rush: 27th in pressure rate and 31st in QB hit rate. Myles Garrett has appeared in only three games. The late surge of four- and five-sack games came against Washington and a bottom-tier Arizona offense.

The bigger problem is the roster from here. Puka Nacua, who drew 93 targets in seven games, is done for the year. Davante Adams is on injured reserve and pointed at mid-December. An offense that passes more than expected at the second-highest rate in the league now has Kyren Williams, Tyler Higbee and Konata Mumpfield as its main targets. Both starting interior linemen, Coleman Shelton and Steve Avila, are out for Green Bay. The run game and the defense have been good enough to win every game since the Arizona upset. The closing stretch has the Chiefs, two Seattle games and a trip to San Francisco, so that formula will be tested before Adams returns.

strengths.title: A run defense that erases offenses
strengths.body: The Rams rank second in rush EPA allowed by play-by-play and fourth in explosive run rate allowed. Opponents can't stay on schedule. Buffalo's 234 rushing yards is the outlier; since then the defense has held Las Vegas, the Chargers, Washington and Arizona to 64 yards or fewer on the ground. This is structural rather than opponent-driven, and it should hold.

strengths.title: Coverage that takes away the end zone
strengths.body: The secondary concedes underneath yards but not big plays or touchdowns. They rank third in deep-pass EPA allowed, fourth on third down and sixth in red-zone TD rate. It's a bend-don't-break shell that wins on efficiency even while the yardage totals look ordinary. Kam Curl's toe injury is the one threat to it.

strengths.title: The league's cleanest pocket and lanes
strengths.body: The line ranks first in pressure rate allowed and first in stuff rate. The backs average 4.69 a carry, fourth in the league, behind a front that gets them 2.8 yards before contact. It drives both the rotation of Williams and Blake Corum and Stafford's low sack rate. The caveat is health: two interior starters are out this week.

concerns.title: The passing game lost its top targets
concerns.body: Nacua's 93 targets were the spine of a pass-first offense that ranks second in pass rate over expected. He won't return this season. Adams is out until roughly mid-December. This is a real flaw for the rest of the year, not noise. Expect McVay to lean harder on the run and on Williams as a receiver, which lowers the ceiling of an offense already down to eleventh in EPA.

concerns.title: Hidden-yardage leaks: kicking units, giveaways
concerns.body: Special teams rank 30th in EPA per game. The offense has 15 turnovers and is minus-3 in turnover differential. These are the main reasons a top-five efficiency team sits at 6-4 with a negative wins-over-expected. Turnover margins tend to drift back toward even. Bad special teams are stickier, and in close games they decide things.

concerns.title: A pass rush that rarely gets home
concerns.body: For all its efficiency, the defense ranks 27th in pressure rate and 31st in QB hit rate, so coverage does almost all the work. Garrett's limited availability is part of it. The recent sack totals came against soft opponents. Against better quarterbacks down the stretch, a coverage-only defense is more likely to give up long drives.

trend.note: A losing record through six weeks, capped by the home upset loss to Arizona, has given way to four straight wins, each one covered. The run ended with a 34-6 rout in Arizona built on 202 rushing yards and five sacks. The underlying play has been good all along; the results have caught up.

nextGame.headline: Rams' elite run defense meets Green Bay's broken ground game
nextGame.body:
The Rams are home after 10 days of rest, favored by 2.5 with a total of 43.5 at the Book. These are two 6-4 teams with different profiles. Green Bay's offense is purely aerial: ninth in pass EPA and dead last in rush EPA. That run game runs into the league's second-best run defense by play-by-play, so expect Jordan Love to carry the whole load against a secondary that rarely allows the deep ball. On the other side, Green Bay's defense wins on turnovers and sacks: second in takeaways, third in sacks, third in turnover differential per game. It has been soft in the red zone (69% TDs allowed, 26th) and on third down. Green Bay's 0.75 one-score win rate and positive wins-over-expected suggest its record is a little ahead of its play.

Availability favors neither side cleanly. The Rams are without Nacua, Adams, center Coleman Shelton and guard Steve Avila. Backup center Dylan McMahon is also on injured reserve, so Stafford is working behind a patched-up interior with a thin receiving group. Kam Curl and Myles Garrett are questionable. Kobie Turner practiced fully, which could help a pass rush that badly needs it. Green Bay is missing Micah Parsons, linebacker Zaire Franklin (a 99% snap player), guard Sean Rhyan and Josh Jacobs. Starting tackle Travis Glover is questionable. Both offensive lines are compromised, which raises the value of whichever defense can actually pressure the quarterback.

waysToWin.title: Make Green Bay one-dimensional early
waysToWin.body: Green Bay is 31st in yards per carry and last in rush EPA, now without Jacobs. Against the Rams' run defense, early downs should go nowhere. That leaves Love in third-and-long against a defense that allows conversions at the fourth-lowest rate in the league. This is the most bankable edge in the game.

waysToWin.title: Feed Kyren Williams in every phase
waysToWin.body: With the top two receivers gone, Williams (51 targets) becomes the offense's focal point. Green Bay ranks 26th in EPA allowed to opposing lead backs and is missing Franklin at linebacker. Screens, swings and a heavy carry share keep Stafford's throws short and away from Green Bay's ball-hawking secondary.

waysToWin.title: Long drives that end in touchdowns
waysToWin.body: The Rams hold the ball (seventh in time of possession) and Green Bay doesn't (26th). Green Bay's red zone defense gives up touchdowns at one of the league's worst rates. Methodical drives finished with sevens instead of field goals would neutralize the Rams' kicking-unit deficit and shorten the game for Love.

waysToLose.title: Handing the ball-hawks extra possessions
waysToLose.body: Green Bay has 19 takeaways, second in the league. The Rams have turned it over in every game but one. Against an offense that can't run, short fields are Green Bay's easiest route to points. Two giveaways would likely flip a game priced this tight.

waysToLose.title: Interior pressure through a patched line
waysToLose.body: Even without Parsons, Green Bay ranks third in sacks. With Shelton and Avila out, the interior that has kept Stafford clean all year is the weakest it has been. If pressure comes up the middle, Stafford has fewer reliable places to go quickly than at any point this season.

waysToLose.title: Love finds the slot with time
waysToLose.body: Green Bay's passing offense ranks ninth in EPA. The Rams have been hit hardest by third receivers, last in the league in PPR allowed over average to WR3s. Their pass rush rarely forces quick throws. A clean pocket against that soft spot is how Green Bay moves the ball without a run game.

nextGame.watch: The Rams' makeshift center-guard combination against Green Bay's sack-heavy front. Stafford, without his top two receivers, needs a clean pocket to function, and that interior is the piece of the line that just lost its starters.

restOfSeason.body:
The efficiency is real: top-five net EPA, a top-four defense and the league's best pass-protecting and run-blocking front when healthy. The record should keep pace with it from here rather than lag. The turnover margin and close-game luck are the parts most likely to even out. Special-teams struggles tend to persist, and they will keep costing a point or two in tight games. The defense, especially against the run, is the sustainable part. Its pass rush won't suddenly become elite.

The offense is where the outlook darkens. Losing Nacua for the year and Adams for at least two or three more weeks pulls a pass-first unit toward a run-and-Williams identity, with less scoring punch. That arrives during the hardest part of the schedule: Kansas City and a trip to San Francisco come before Adams is likely back. San Francisco is well clear in the division, so this is a wild-card push. Two games against Seattle, level at 6-4, will likely decide the Rams' seeding, if not their playoff ticket. Expect a low-scoring, defense-led finish with a record close to their efficiency, somewhere around double-digit wins.
swingFactors: Timing and form of Davante Adams' return
Health of the interior line (Shelton, Avila)
Whether the turnover margin finally evens out

confidence.note: Ten games of efficient play, but season-altering receiver and line injuries change the offense.
